title: Ben Johnson: Players are ‘fighting to be on that grass and help us win’ | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Williams did not practice Saturday, and Tyson Bagent is cleared and in a QB1/QB2 mix for Monday night; the coach won't name the starter until the week plays out.
summary: Coach Ben Johnson said the week has gone well, though there is still uncertainty about who will be active for Monday night. Tyson Bagent was cleared, returned to meetings Friday, and was set to practice Saturday, which Johnson called good for him. Caleb Williams was not practicing Saturday, and Johnson said he needed to see something from everyone on a big day. Johnson said the QB pecking order would stay fluid, with a decision coming after the week's plan plays out. He described Bagent as a cerebral, mentally prepared backup who could be the backup or part of the starting conversation, and said both QBs bring different skill sets. Tyrique Stevenson participated more than expected after a summer injury, and Johnson praised his toughness. Ozzy Trapilo will not play Monday. Kicker Cairo Santos is practicing Saturday and is expected to be available Monday, and a kickoff-rule discrepancy is expected to be resolved in a call that afternoon. Johnson also discussed his relationship with a veteran coach he brought in from New Orleans, saying he is a seasoned, accountable mentor.

title: Exclusive: Kellen Moore previews Saints' home opener vs. Raiders
headline: Asim Richards is set to replace Kelvin Banks on the Saints' offensive line for the Raiders game, with Kellen Moore saying he'll have a full week to prepare.
summary: Kellen Moore framed the home opener in the Caesars Superdome as a chance to build atmosphere, with the crowd feeding off strong play on the field. He said the team needs to execute well so the fans can get behind it. On the Raiders, who are 2-0 and tied for the league lead in sacks, Moore called them very talented, especially their four-man rush and pressure schemes. The Saints will need awareness, quick ball release, and solid protection. Asked about Asim Richards stepping in for Kelvin Banks, Moore pointed to Richards' work last year and his strong performance against Baltimore, and said he'll have a full week to get ready. On Kirk Cousins, Moore called him steady and calm, saying teammates play at a higher level around him, and credited Las Vegas for a strong start.

signals.claim: Will start in place of Kelvin Banks against the Raiders, with a full week of preparation.
signals.note: Richards is an offensive lineman, so this is mainly a depth and line-stability note with limited direct fantasy value.

topics.detail: The Raiders are 2-0 and lead the league in sacks. Moore said their front four and pressure packages require ball-security awareness and quick throws from the Saints.
Moore is looking forward to the first home game in the Superdome and sees the crowd as a factor when the team plays well.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: September 26, 2026
headline: Jonathan Greenard had a good week but is still limited in practice, with his status to be decided after the final session; Makai Lemon's touches are expected to grow.
summary: Sirianni said the team had a good week of practice overall, with one more practice day left before the Chicago trip, and that the tight ends in general had a good week. He called Jonathan Greenard's week good, said he brings energy and leadership from the sideline, and said the team would see where he stands at the end of Friday's practice. On Zach Ertz, he said Ertz had a good week, and he described the process of getting players who missed camp caught up on habits like tackling, strip attempts, and ball security. For Makai Lemon, Sirianni said he is improving each week, that the team wants individual success but team success comes first, and that his touches will come because he does the right thing when the ball is not going to him. He credited DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks for a good start and said Lemon's contributions don't show on the stat sheet. On the quarterback question, he praised Jalen Hurts as a partner. On play action, he said the sample size is small and the team is still figuring out its identity, and that the offense has been behind schedule too often to rely on play action. On the new interior linemen, he said Drew Kendall at center and a left guard in a new spot had a good week of preparation and need one more good practice. He declined to say much about the kickoff 12th-man issue beyond saying everything the team does is within the rules.
